articles.title: Three Short Lines in the Margin
articles.summary: After marking every correct answer, a teacher notices that the same small drawing has been hiding in the margin.
articles.summaryZh: 一名教师批完所有正确答案后，才注意到同一幅小图一直躲在页边。
storyParagraphs: Teacher Lin marked quickly. Correct answers received circles, mistakes received dots, and the most common error became the next day's review. Rui'an's workbook was almost all circles, but he kept drawing three short lines with four small spaces beneath them in the margin. Teacher Lin assumed he was distracted and moved on.

During a measurement lesson, Rui'an described a strip four units long as five. Two days later, he said the distance from three to seven on a number line was five. One answer was right and one wrong, yet the same little drawing appeared beside both.

At lunch, Teacher Lin did not ask him to repeat the whole page. She placed a ruler on the desk and asked him to show how many intervals lay between two marks. Rui'an counted the marks themselves: 'One, two, three, four, five.' He was counting endpoints rather than the distance between them.

That afternoon, Teacher Lin drew chalk lines across the floor. The class stood on one line and counted the steps needed to reach another. She did not announce that this was Rui'an's mistake. After taking four steps, he turned, looked at the five lines on the floor, and opened his workbook to the earlier page.
After school, Teacher Lin drew a small circle beside the sketch in the margin. The next day, she looked at the drawing before she looked at the answer.
storyParagraphsZh: 林老师批改得很快。对的画圈，错的打点，第二天先讲错得最多的一题。瑞安的练习册几乎全是圈，他却总在页边画三道短线，下面再添四个小格。林老师以为那只是走神，没有多看。
测量课上，瑞安把一段四格长的木条写成五格。两天后的数轴题，他又把从三到七的距离算成五。答案一对一错，页边却都有那三道短线和四个小格。
午休时，林老师没有把他留下重做整页，只把一把尺放在桌上，请他指出“从这里到这里”有几段。瑞安依次数过刻度线：“一、二、三、四、五。”他数的是端点，不是端点之间的距离。
下午，林老师把粉笔线画在地上，让全班站在线上，再问跨过几段才到另一边。她没有说这是瑞安的错误。瑞安走了四步，回头看了看地上的五条线，把练习册翻回前一页。
放学后，林老师在那幅页边小图旁画了一个小圈。第二天批改时，她先看了图，再看答案。
explanationParagraphs: Teacher noticing means selectively attending to classroom evidence, interpreting it through knowledge of the subject and learning, and choosing an appropriate response. It is more than general attentiveness, and not every error requires immediate whole-class correction. The important clues are those that reveal the thinking a learner is using and allow a teacher to test that interpretation.
explanationParagraphsZh: 教师察觉是有选择地关注课堂线索，结合学科与学习知识解释其意义，再决定合适回应。它不等于一般细心，也不是发现任何错误就立即全班纠正。关键在于辨认哪些细节揭示了学习者正在使用的思路，并用回应继续检验这一判断。

articles.title: Three Small Tables in the Classroom
articles.summary: A teacher keeps adding separate tables for pupils who cannot access the main lesson until the class sits farther and farther apart.
articles.summaryZh: 一位教师不断为跟不上主课的孩子另开小桌，直到教室里的人越坐越远。
storyParagraphs: When Teacher Gu taught rivers, she hung one detailed map high on the wall. A-Ting, who could not see it clearly, sat at a small table by the window while an assistant explained it again. Mia, still learning the local language, sat near the door with simplified cards. Zhou Ke, who found writing difficult, waited until after class to answer aloud. Teacher Gu worked hard, but the number of separate tables kept growing.

Before a spring outing, the class had to plan a route to the river mouth together. Pupils at the main table knew only the wall map. The three at the smaller tables each held useful information, but they had never taken part in the same discussion. Half a lesson passed and the class still could not decide which shallows to avoid.

The next day, Teacher Gu put away the wall map and spread a large raised map across a low table. Place names appeared in print, colour, and recorded sound. Pupils could draw a route, arrange wooden pieces, or explain aloud, but everyone answered the same question: how could the whole class reach the river mouth safely?

A-Ting felt a sharp bend that was easy to miss by sight. Mia recognised a ferry name from its sound marker. Zhou Ke moved wooden pieces to connect both discoveries to the route. The other pupils gathered around the same table and revised their plans.
After the outing, Teacher Gu pushed together the three small tables from the window, door, and back of the room. She did not put their name labels back.
storyParagraphsZh: 顾老师讲河流时，只在高处挂一张细密的地图。看不清的阿庭被安排到窗边小桌，听助教重新说明；刚学本地语言的米娅坐在门旁，用另一套简化卡片；手不方便握笔的周可则等下课后口头回答。顾老师很用心，教室里的小桌却越来越多。
春游前，全班要一起规划去河口的路线。主桌上的孩子只会看墙图，小桌上的三个人各自掌握一部分信息，却从没参加同一场讨论。大家争了半节课，仍无法决定该避开哪段浅滩。
第二天，顾老师收起墙图，把一张带有凸起河道的大地图铺在低桌上。地点名称既有文字，也有颜色和声音标记。学生可以画路线、摆木片或口头说明理由，但都要回答同一个问题：怎样让全班安全抵达河口。
阿庭摸到一处地图上没有明显画出的急弯；米娅从声音标记里听出渡口名称；周可移动木片，把两人的发现连进路线。其他学生围在同一张桌旁修改自己的方案。
春游回来后，顾老师把窗边、门旁和讲台后的三张小桌搬到一起。桌上的姓名牌没有再放回去。
explanationParagraphs: Inclusive pedagogy responds to learner differences by expanding shared opportunities to access information, participate, and express understanding while retaining meaningful challenge. It does not deny the need for individual support. Instead, it resists separation as the default response and makes support part of the common classroom design wherever possible.
explanationParagraphsZh: 全纳教学法通过扩展所有学习者都能进入的共同学习机会来回应差异，包括信息呈现、参与方式与成果表达的多样性，同时保持有意义的挑战。它不否认个别支持的必要，而是不把分离当成默认答案，并尽量让支持成为共同课堂设计的一部分。

articles.title: The Ten Minutes Lost Each Day
articles.summary: A teacher urges the class to move faster every day without ever making the next step predictable.
articles.summaryZh: 一位教师每天都在催全班快一点，却从未让任何人知道下一步该做什么。
storyParagraphs: At the start of the second lesson each morning, Teacher Cheng began calling, 'Put away the brushes, hand in the pictures, collect the number boards, and sit in pairs.' Some pupils washed brushes first, others queued with paintings, and a few already had boards on their desks. By the time the last water cup was stored, the minute hand had moved ten marks.

Teacher Cheng spoke more loudly and made her instructions longer. The children still asked the same questions every day: where should paintings go, who collected wet brushes, and which cupboard held the boards? During an open lesson, visiting teachers were already seated at the back while the class searched for one missing board.

That afternoon, Teacher Cheng did not begin a new topic. She and the pupils walked through the changeover itself. At each table, one child collected brushes, one delivered the paintings, and the others fetched boards. Wet work went on the window rack. Anyone finished early checked three small pictures beside the door. The first rehearsal was still slow, the second exposed forgotten roles, and the third needed no questions.

When the second-lesson bell rang the next day, Teacher Cheng stood beside the board without giving an instruction. The children checked the pictures and moved. The final number board was in place after the minute hand had advanced only three marks.
Teacher Cheng picked up the chalk to begin, then put it down again and pressed flat the curling corner of the second picture by the door.
storyParagraphsZh: 每到上午第二节课，程老师就开始催：“收画笔，交作品，拿算术板，两人一组坐好。”有人先去洗笔，有人排队交画，还有人已经把算术板铺开。等最后一只水杯收好，墙上的分针总会走过十格。
程老师说得越来越响，也把指令写得越来越长。孩子们仍然每天询问同样的问题：画放在哪里，湿笔谁来收，算术板从哪一柜取。一次公开课上，来访老师已经坐在后排，全班还在寻找少了一块的板子。
那天下午，程老师没有开始新课。她和孩子们把转换过程实际走了一遍：每桌一人收笔，一人送画，其余人取板；湿画放在窗边架上；做完的人看门旁的三幅小图。第一次练习仍很慢，第二次有人忘了换角色，第三次才没有人开口问。
第二天，第二节课的钟声响起。程老师站在讲台旁，没有发出指令。孩子们看了门旁的小图，各自起身。最后一块算术板放稳时，分针只走过三格。
程老师拿起粉笔准备上课，又放下它，把门旁第二幅已经卷边的小图重新贴平。
explanationParagraphs: Classroom routines establish predictable, explicitly taught, and practised ways to handle recurring activities. They reduce uncertainty, coordination costs, and unnecessary demands on attention, leaving more capacity for learning. Effective routines are not merely obedience: their purpose should be clear, responsibility can be shared, and the routine should change when classroom needs change.
explanationParagraphsZh: 课堂常规是对反复发生的活动建立可预测、经过明确教授与练习的行动方式。它能减少转换中的不确定性、协调成本和注意消耗，让教师与学生把心力留给学习。有效常规并非单纯服从，也需要说明目的、分担责任，并随课堂需要调整。

articles.title: The Sun Inside the Shadow
articles.summary: An astronomer can calculate every movement of a shadow but cannot teach children to draw the sun on the correct side.
articles.summaryZh: 一名天文学家能算出日影的每次移动，却始终教不会孩子把太阳画在正确的一边。
storyParagraphs: Dr Yan could calculate the sunrise for any day of the year. Invited to teach shadows at the town school, he drew solar height, angles, and paths. The children copied every formula. Yet in the next day's quiz, half of them still placed the sun at the far end of the shadow.

Dr Yan explained the lesson again with a more precise diagram. The children nodded, but their answers did not change. While collecting the papers, he found a sentence in one margin: 'The sun makes the shadow, so the shadow must follow the sun.' That sentence was nowhere in his lecture.

That afternoon, Dr Yan placed a lamp low on a table with several wooden figures. He asked the children to predict where the shadows would fall before letting them move the lamp. One pupil put the lamp on the shadow side, and the dark shape immediately jumped in the opposite direction. For the first time, someone erased the sun from their drawing.

The class then traced the flagpole's shadow in the yard every hour. The formulas remained on the board, but each line now had a question beside it: Which side is the sun on now? What happens to the shadow if the lamp rises?
At the end of the lesson, Dr Yan left his most accurate path diagram behind. Beside it, he pinned the children's first drawing with the sun in the wrong place.
storyParagraphsZh: 严博士能算出一年中任何一天的日出时刻。镇学校请他讲影子时，他画了太阳高度、角度和轨迹，孩子们也把公式完整抄下。可第二天的小测里，半数人仍把太阳画在影子末端。
严博士又讲了一遍，换了更精确的图。孩子们点头，答案却没有改变。他收卷时发现，一个学生在页边写着：“影子是太阳照出来的，所以应该追着太阳走。”这句话不在他的讲稿里。
下午，严博士把一盏灯放在低桌上，又摆了几个木偶。他先让孩子们猜影子会落在哪里，再允许他们移动灯。有人把灯放到影子那一侧，桌上的黑影立刻跑到了相反方向。教室里第一次有人擦掉自己的太阳。
接着，他让孩子们在院里每隔一小时描一次旗杆的影子。公式仍在黑板上，但每条线旁都多了一个问题：太阳此刻在哪一边？如果灯升高，影子会怎样？
课程结束后，严博士没有带走那张最精确的轨迹图。他把学生第一张画错太阳的位置贴在旁边。
explanationParagraphs: Pedagogical content knowledge is the specialised knowledge used to turn particular subject matter into representations, examples, tasks, and questions that specific learners can understand. It includes awareness of common difficulties and misconceptions. Deep subject expertise does not automatically produce effective teaching; educators also need to know how learners interpret the topic and what experiences can change that interpretation.
explanationParagraphsZh: 学科教学知识是把具体学科内容转化成特定学习者能够理解的表示、案例、任务与问题的专门知识，也包括对常见困难和错误观念的认识。深厚学科知识并不会自动产生有效教学；教师还需知道学习者如何理解这一内容，以及什么经验能促使理解改变。

articles.title: The Wager on the Heavy Stone
articles.summary: Pupils can recite the correct answer yet still bet their lunch on the heavy stone landing first.
articles.summaryZh: 学生们能背出正确答案，却仍把午饭押在那块一定会先落地的重石上。
storyParagraphs: By the end of the physics lesson, the whole class could repeat the conclusion written on the board. At lunch, however, they gathered below the tower and made a wager: if a heavy stone and a light one were released together, the heavy stone would certainly land first. A-Luo even bet his apple.

The teacher did not ask them to copy the conclusion again. She asked A-Luo to write down his prediction and explain it. 'Heavy things feel a greater force, so they must travel faster,' he wrote. Several classmates signed their names beneath his answer.

They first dropped two clay balls of the same size but different weight. The sounds of impact nearly overlapped. A-Luo said the tower was not high enough. The teacher then released a coin and a flat sheet of paper. The paper fell much more slowly, and the pupils immediately gave the victory back to weight.

The teacher crushed the paper into a tight ball and released it beside the coin. This time, both struck the wooden board together. A-Luo picked up the paper, looked at its broad shape when unfolded, and crossed out half of his explanation.
That afternoon, he did not erase his original wager. He added a new prediction underneath it and put the apple back in his schoolbag.
storyParagraphsZh: 物理课结束时，全班都能背出老师写在黑板上的结论。可午休时，他们仍在塔下打赌：一块重石和一块轻石同时松手，重石一定先落地。阿洛甚至押上了自己的苹果。
老师没有再让他们抄结论。她请阿洛先把赌注写在纸上，并说明原因。阿洛写道：“重的东西受力更大，所以会跑得更快。”其他人纷纷签名赞同。
他们先丢下两颗大小相同、重量不同的泥球。两声落地几乎重叠。阿洛说塔不够高。老师又拿出一枚硬币和一张纸，纸果然慢得多。孩子们立刻把胜负归给重量。
老师把那张纸揉成紧实的小团，再与硬币同时放手。这一次，两样东西一同敲在木板上。阿洛捡起纸团，看看它展开后的宽面，又把自己的理由划掉一半。
下午，他没有擦掉最初的赌注。阿洛在下面添了一行新预测，把苹果放回书包。
explanationParagraphs: Misconception diagnosis looks for the reasoning model that repeatedly produces a class of answers rather than merely marking right and wrong. Predictions, explanations, confidence, and carefully chosen contrasts help distinguish a stable alternative idea from an accidental mistake. Teaching can respond effectively only after the learner's active explanation has become visible.
explanationParagraphsZh: 错误概念诊断寻找的是持续产生某类答案的推理模型，而非只标记对错。预测、理由、信心和经过选择的对照情境，可以区分稳定误解与偶然失误。只有看见学习者实际调用的解释，教学才能设计出会触动该解释的证据与任务。

articles.title: Three Pens on the Same Page
articles.summary: Three apprentices read the same harbour record and stop at entirely different parts of the page.
articles.summaryZh: 三名学徒读完同一份港口记录，却各自停在了完全不同的地方。
storyParagraphs: Three classes at the academy received the same old harbour record. It listed a ship's arrival time, the temperature of its hold, a night watchman's signature, and a penalty that had been altered. Every class was asked for the main idea. Their answers were nearly identical: a ship had been fined because its cargo was damaged.

A few days later, the harbour office asked the academy to determine how the loss had actually occurred. Anlan, studying history, checked who wrote the record, when additions were made, and whether the watchman's signature matched another duty book. Taoyu, studying chemistry, circled the temperature and cargo name and looked up how that material changed under heat. Miko, studying law, followed the altered penalty and asked who had authority to revise it.

When the three met again, none tried to summarise the whole page. Anlan found that the record had been written two days late. Taoyu found that the stated temperature could not have caused the damage. Miko uncovered an old rule requiring shipowners to report breakage themselves.

With their markings laid together, a different sequence appeared: the owner may first have concealed the damage, the watchman recorded it later, and the changed penalty obscured when the report was made. Their teacher set the neat original summary to one side and did not ask anyone to copy it again.
Before returning the record, each apprentice wrote a question in a different colour along the margin. The old sheet was still one page, but its edges were no longer empty.
storyParagraphsZh: 学院发给三个班同一页旧港口记录。上面写着船只到岸时间、货舱温度、守夜人的签名和一笔被涂改的罚款。老师要求所有人概括中心意思。三个班交上来的答案几乎一样：一艘船因货物受损而被处罚。
几天后，港务局请学院判断那次损失究竟怎么发生。学历史的安岚先查记录由谁写、何时补写，又把守夜人的签名与另一份值班簿相比。学化学的陶宇圈出温度和货物名称，去找同种材料受热后的变化。学法律的米珂只盯着被涂改的罚款，追查当时允许谁改动处罚。
三个人重新坐到一起时，谁也没有“概括”整页。安岚发现记录晚写了两天；陶宇发现记录中的温度不足以造成损坏；米珂则找到一条要求船主自行报告破损的旧规。
他们把三种标记叠在一起，才看见船主可能先隐瞒破损，守夜人后来补记，而罚款改动掩盖了报告时间。老师把最初那句整齐的中心意思放在桌边，没有再请人誊清。
归还记录前，三名学徒各用一种颜色把自己的问题写在页边。旧纸只有一页，边缘却再也不是空的。
explanationParagraphs: Disciplinary literacy refers to the specialised ways fields use words, numbers, images, and symbols to build and test knowledge. Different disciplines attend to different clues, ask different questions, and apply different standards of credibility. General comprehension remains useful, but deeper reading requires understanding why particular features matter within a field and how that field judges a claim.
explanationParagraphsZh: 学科读写能力是各领域使用文字、数字、图像与符号来建构和检验知识的专门方式。不同学科关注的线索、提问和可信标准并不相同。一般概括策略仍有价值，但深入阅读还要求理解本领域为何重视某些特征，以及怎样判断主张成立。

articles.title: Two Accusations in the Same Face
articles.summary: Missing a crucial reaction shot, an editor borrows a silent face from an older reel.
articles.summaryZh: 剪辑师缺少一个关键反应镜头，便从旧胶片里借来一张沉默的脸。
storyParagraphs: The city news house was due to screen a report about a theft that evening, but editor Peiluo had no shot of the shopkeeper hearing the news. His producer demanded the film on time. In an older reel, Peiluo found a close-up of the man sitting by a doorway. He said nothing and lifted his eyes once.

Peiluo first placed the face after a shot of the empty cash box. Preview viewers said the shopkeeper looked guilty. Then he placed it after a shot of the weeping assistant. The same face now seemed restrained by grief. Not one frame of the close-up had changed.

The producer chose the first version because it felt 'stronger'. After the screening, the shopkeeper's daughter came to the news house. She recognised the old coat and said the close-up had been filmed six months earlier during a winter-clothing appeal. Her father had not even been present at the theft.

Peiluo hung both versions on the editing rack and turned the handle again and again. The cash box, the silent face, and the crying assistant were all images the camera had truly recorded. In a new order, however, they gave the shopkeeper a reaction that had never occurred.
Before the second screening, Peiluo removed the close-up and left the empty seconds on the screen.
storyParagraphsZh: 城里的新闻馆要在当晚放映一段失窃案报道，剪辑师裴洛却缺少店主听见消息后的反应。制片人催他按时交片。裴洛从旧胶片里找到店主坐在门边的一张近景：没有说话，只抬了一次眼。
他先把这张脸接在空钱匣之后。试看片的人都说，店主像是在心虚。裴洛又试着把它接在哭泣的伙计之后，同一张脸立刻显得悲伤而克制。镜头本身一帧没变。
制片人选择了第一版，因为“更有力”。放映后，店主的女儿来到新闻馆。她认出那件旧外套，说这段近景拍于半年前的冬衣募捐，父亲当时根本不在失窃现场。
裴洛把两版胶片同时挂上剪辑架，一遍遍转动手柄。钱匣、沉默的脸、哭泣的伙计，各自都是真实拍到的画面；它们换过位置以后，却替店主生出了一段从未发生的反应。
第二场放映开始前，裴洛拆下那张近景，把空出的几秒留在银幕上。
explanationParagraphs: Montage constructs meaning through the selection, order, duration, and juxtaposition of shots. Viewers infer emotion, time, space, and causation across cuts, so the same image can support opposite readings in different contexts. Editing can clarify an event, but it can also arrange truthful images into a meaning that never occurred.
explanationParagraphsZh: 蒙太奇通过镜头的选择、顺序、时长和并置建构意义。观众会跨越剪切推断情绪、时间、空间与因果，因此同一镜头放在不同前后关系中可能产生相反解释。剪辑既能澄清事件，也能把真实画面组织成并未发生的含义。

articles.title: The Bell Only the Audience Could Hear
articles.summary: A sound editor adds a bell to a chase and accidentally lets the fugitive know something he should not know.
articles.summaryZh: 声音师为追逐戏添了一声钟，却让银幕上的逃亡者突然知道了不该知道的事。
storyParagraphs: A rooftop chase already moved quickly, but the director felt it lacked something. At the instant the fugitive turned his head, sound editor Luoqi added a low bell. She meant it only to unsettle the audience, like a drum inside the score.

After the preview, viewers asked, 'Once he hears the alarm bell, why doesn't he run out of the city?' Others wondered why the guards behind him did not react. Luoqi explained that the bell did not exist inside that city. This only confused them further, because the man on screen turned at the exact moment it rang.

She muted the track and watched the original footage. The actor had turned because someone on set called for a stop; the editor had kept the moment as hesitation. Once the bell was added, the turn gained a new cause. The fugitive now seemed to know that an alarm had already been raised.

Luoqi moved the bell earlier, but the image still suggested that someone heard it. At last, she replaced it with strings that had no visible source and saved the real city bell for the later shot in which a guard struck it.
At the public screening, the fugitive turned once again. The strings rose beyond the screen, while the city around him remained silent.
storyParagraphsZh: 一场屋顶追逐拍得很紧张，导演仍觉得少了点什么。声音师洛琪在逃亡者回头的瞬间加进一声低沉的钟。那声音原本只是为了让观众不安，就像配乐里的鼓点。
试映结束后，观众却问：“他听见警钟以后，为什么不往城外跑？”还有人问，追在后面的守卫为什么没有反应。洛琪解释钟并不在那座城里，观众反而更困惑，因为银幕上的人恰好在钟声响起时回了头。
她关掉声音重看原片。演员回头，是因为拍摄现场有人喊停；剪辑时，那一瞬被留下来当作犹豫。钟声盖上去以后，回头便有了新的原因，也让角色像是提前知道警报已经发出。
洛琪试着把钟移到更早的位置，画面仍像有人听见。最后，她换成一段没有明确声源的弦乐，把真正的城钟留到守卫敲响它的镜头。
正式放映时，逃亡者再次回头。银幕外的弦音升高，城里仍然安静。
explanationParagraphs: Diegetic sound belongs to the story world and can in principle be heard by its characters. Non-diegetic sound is supplied only to the audience, as with external music or narration. Whether a source is visible does not alone decide the category. The choice changes what characters know, why events occur, and how viewers understand space and point of view.
explanationParagraphsZh: 叙事内声属于作品呈现的故事世界，角色原则上可能听见；叙事外声只提供给观众，如外部配乐或旁白。声源是否出现在画面中并不能单独决定其身份。两者的选择会改变角色知道什么、事件为何发生以及观众如何理解空间与视点。

articles.title: The People on the Right of the Frame
articles.summary: A filmmaker captures a perfect harvest festival while leaving the people waiting by the bridge outside the picture.
articles.summaryZh: 一名摄影师拍下了完美的丰收庆典，也把桥边等待的人群留在了画面之外。
storyParagraphs: On harvest day, the city hall hired Li Qing to make a short film about the celebration. Flags filled the square and dancers moved along the main street. On the right, however, an old bridge had closed without warning. Grain carriers crowded behind the barrier, complaining that the repair notice had arrived too late.

Li Qing wanted a clean image, so she moved the camera left. Inside the frame were only dancers, flags, and carts already filled with grain. The argument by the bridge remained audible, so she changed to a closer shot and covered the voices with festival drums.

After the screening, the city hall described the day as a smooth arrival for the whole town. Li Qing's brother returned from a journey and asked why she had not filmed him. He had spent four hours beside the bridge with a cart of apples, half of which spoiled in the sun.

Li Qing went back to the editing room and found a wide shot recorded while she changed position. The dancers crossed on the left while grain carts stood in a line on the right. Both had happened on the same afternoon. She removed none of the celebration, but restored those seconds to the opening.
Before the second screening, Li Qing pulled the curtains on both sides of the screen a hand's width farther apart.
storyParagraphsZh: 丰收节那天，市政厅请黎青拍一段城市影片。广场挂满彩旗，舞队沿主街前进。右侧的旧桥却临时关闭，许多运粮人堵在栏杆外，抱怨修桥通知来得太晚。
黎青想让画面整齐，便把机位向左移。取景框里只剩舞队、旗帜和装满粮食的车。桥边的争吵仍能听见，她又换了一个更近的镜头，把声音也盖进鼓乐里。
影片放映后，市政厅称那天“全城顺利入市”。黎青的弟弟却从外地回来，问她为什么没有拍到自己。他那天推着一车苹果，在桥边等了四个小时，最后半车都被晒坏。
黎青回到剪辑室，找到一段换机位时留下的宽画面。左边舞队经过，右边粮车停成一线，两件事发生在同一个下午。她没有删掉任何庆典，只把那几秒接回了影片开头。
第二次放映前，黎青把银幕两侧的帷幕又向外拉开了一掌。
explanationParagraphs: Framing uses image boundaries, camera position, scale, and composition to determine what viewers see and what remains outside the picture. Every frame is selective. It establishes emphasis while also shaping interpretation. Responsible image-making asks when excluded context is substantial enough to change the meaning of what is shown.
explanationParagraphsZh: 取景与框架通过画面边界、机位、尺度和构图决定观众看见什么，以及哪些信息留在画外。任何框架都具有选择性；它既建立重点，也会改变事件解释。负责任的影像需要意识到被排除的部分何时足以改变整体意义。

articles.title: The Door Everyone Pulled the Wrong Way
articles.summary: An award-winning bronze door stops every visitor while its designer first blames them for ignoring the sign.
articles.summaryZh: 一扇获奖的青铜门让每位访客停在门口，设计师却先责怪他们没有看告示。
storyParagraphs: The new city hall had a bronze entrance designed by Shen Tuo. He fitted it with two elegant vertical handles and won a prize before the building even opened. The first visitor grasped a handle and pulled. The door did not move. The second visitor pulled as well, and a queue soon formed behind them.

Shen Tuo posted a sign saying PUSH. People who noticed it began using their shoulders, while anyone carrying a box still reached for the handles first. On rainy days, the paper became unreadable and visitors went back to pulling. Shen Tuo decided that people simply refused to pay attention.

One day, while recording damage in the entrance hall, he watched a child run toward a side door. Its outer face had no handle, only a flat bronze plate. The child naturally pushed it open. At the main entrance, however, the same child seized the vertical handle and pulled.

After closing time, Shen Tuo removed the outer handles and installed a flat plate. He kept a horizontal bar on the inside so that people leaving could push their way out. The next morning, no one stopped to read instructions and no one struck the door with a shoulder.
Shen Tuo peeled away the curling PUSH sign and left no new words in its place.
storyParagraphsZh: 新市政厅装了一扇青铜门。设计师沈拓为它做了两根漂亮的竖把手，开幕前还因此得了奖。第一位访客握住把手向外拉，门没有动。第二位也拉。后面的人很快排成了队。
沈拓在门上贴了一张“请推”。有人看见后改用肩膀顶门，手里抱着箱子的人仍会先抓住把手。雨天，纸告示被打湿，访客又开始拉。沈拓认定大家只是不肯仔细看。
一天，他站在门厅记录损坏，看到一个孩子跑向侧门。侧门外侧没有把手，只有一块平铜板。孩子自然伸手推开了。回到正门，他却握住竖把手往回拉。
闭馆后，沈拓拆掉正门外侧的竖把手，换上一块平板；内侧则保留横杆，让离开的人可以一推便开。第二天，没有人停在门前读说明，也没有人用肩膀撞门。
沈拓最后揭下那张已经卷边的“请推”，门上没有留下新的字。
explanationParagraphs: An affordance is a possibility for action created by the relationship between an object's or environment's features and an actor's abilities. A signifier indicates where or how to act. Effective design aligns perceptible cues with the action that is actually available. When form repeatedly invites the wrong behaviour, changing the object is often better than adding instructions.
explanationParagraphsZh: 可供性是物体或环境特征与行动者能力相遇时形成的行动可能；意符则提示人在何处、怎样行动。有效设计让可感知线索与真实可用的动作一致。若形状不断诱导错误行为，增加文字说明往往不如改变物体本身。

articles.title: The Award-Winning Workbench
articles.summary: A perfectly drawn workbench enters a joinery, and within weeks every craftsperson discovers a different way to hurt.
articles.summaryZh: 一张线条完美的工作台进了木工作坊，几周后，每个人都找到了不同的疼法。
storyParagraphs: The city installed a row of new workbenches at the East River joinery. The tops were broad, the drawers symmetrical, and every tool followed a straight line on the plan. The designer had won a prize for them. On the first day, the craftspeople admired their beauty, and the owner hoped the benches would help complete the winter orders.

Two weeks later, the shorter A-He had to lift her shoulders whenever she planed wood. Tall Master Meng bent so low that he needed the table edge to stand upright. Left-handed workers twisted to the right each time they reached the sharpening stone. The owner posted a diagram of 'correct posture'. The pain remained, while the number of spoiled joints increased.

When the designer came to inspect, he insisted that every dimension met the standard. A-He handed him her apron and asked him to finish one drawer at the lowest station. Within half an hour, his wrist pressed painfully against the edge. At Master Meng's bench, his own shoulder blocked the lamp.

The benches were not discarded. The designer gave the tops three height settings, made the tool racks movable from side to side, and placed frequently used stones on a turntable. Workers could change sides during long tasks, while a sliding support brought heavy boards within reach.
Before beginning the next set of drawers, A-He pressed the adjustment bar. The top rose just below her elbow. She lowered her shoulders before picking up the plane.
storyParagraphsZh: 城里给河东木工作坊换了一排新工作台。台面宽阔、抽屉对称，所有工具都按图纸排成直线，设计师还凭它得了奖。师傅们第一天都说漂亮，坊主也希望靠它赶完冬季订单。
两周后，个子矮的阿禾总要抬着肩膀刨木；高个子的孟师傅弯腰久了，起身要扶桌沿。左手用刀的人必须把身体拧向右侧才能够到磨石。坊主贴出“保持正确姿势”的图，疼痛并没有消失，做坏的榫头反而多了。
设计师来检查时，坚持尺寸符合标准。阿禾把自己的围裙交给他，请他在最矮的位置完成一只抽屉。不到半个时辰，他的手腕便抵住了桌边。换到孟师傅的位置，灯光又被自己的肩膀挡住。
新工作台没有被丢掉。设计师把台面改成三档高度，让工具架能够左右移动，又把需要反复取用的磨石放进转盘。工作每隔一段时间可以换边，重木板则由滑架送到手边。
下一批抽屉开工前，阿禾踩下调节杆。台面升到她的肘下，她松开肩膀，才拿起刨刀。
explanationParagraphs: Ergonomics uses knowledge of human physical, perceptual, and cognitive differences and limitations to design tasks, tools, and workplaces. Its purpose is not merely comfort or one prescribed posture, but a better fit between people and work that reduces injury and error while supporting reliable performance. Adjustability, duration, recovery, and work organisation can all matter.
explanationParagraphsZh: 人体工学依据人的身体、感知、认知差异与限制来设计任务、工具和工作环境。目标不只是舒适或固定的“正确姿势”，而是改善人与工作的适配，降低伤害和错误，并支持可靠表现。可调节性、工作持续时间、恢复与组织方式都可能重要。

articles.title: Three Materials Before the Storm
articles.summary: A lampmaker resents the harbour's narrow contest rules until a storm leaves no replacement for his invented parts.
articles.summaryZh: 一名制灯师嫌港口的比赛规则太窄，直到他在风雨里找不到自己发明的零件。
storyParagraphs: Each year, the harbour chose a storm lamp. A young maker named Gu Yan entered an intricate design: an imported spring adjusted the wick, thin crystal threw light far across the water, and the casing used a light alloy that only he knew how to mix. It won easily.

The first winter storm cracked the crystal, while salt mist seized the spring. The lighthouse keeper searched the stores and found only ordinary glass, copper sheet, and old sailcloth. Gu Yan lived three days away. The lamp remained dark for two nights when it was needed most.

The following year's contest allowed only those three materials and required the keeper to replace any part within fifteen minutes. Gu Yan said this was not design but a way of tying a maker's hands. He considered withdrawing, yet the harbour order would pay his apprentices through the winter.

He replaced the automatic spring with flexible copper, used sailcloth as a wind seal, and made every glass pane removable from the same opening. The new lamp was heavier and less brilliant, but it could be opened while wearing wet gloves.

During the next storm, a pane cracked again. The keeper took ordinary glass from the shelf, slid out the broken piece, and installed the new one. By the time Gu Yan arrived, the lamp was already burning.
storyParagraphsZh: 港口每年选一盏暴风灯。年轻制灯师顾岩带来一件精巧作品：进口弹簧能自动调节灯芯，薄水晶把光放得很远，外壳则用了只有他会配的轻合金。他毫无悬念地得了第一。
入冬后的第一场风暴打裂了水晶，盐雾又卡住弹簧。守塔人翻遍仓库，只找到普通玻璃、铜片和旧帆布。顾岩住在三日外的城里，灯在最需要的时候熄了两个晚上。
第二年，比赛只准使用港口常备的三种材料，还要求守塔人能在一刻钟内拆换。顾岩认为这不是设计，而是在绑住设计师的手。他本想退出，可港口订单正够支付学徒们一冬的工钱。
他把自动弹簧换成可弯的铜片，用帆布做防风垫圈，又让每块玻璃都能从同一处抽出。新灯没有上一盏轻，也不够耀眼，却能在戴着湿手套时拆开。
暴风夜里，一块玻璃再次裂了。守塔人从架上取下普通玻璃，抽出旧片，换上新片。顾岩赶到时，灯已经重新亮了。
explanationParagraphs: Design constraints are requirements and boundaries that define feasible solutions, including user needs, safety, materials, maintenance conditions, cost, and time. Real constraints expose trade-offs and can prompt more suitable designs. Constraints should still be examined: designers must distinguish fixed conditions from assumptions that have never been questioned.
explanationParagraphsZh: 设计约束是限定可行方案的要求与边界，例如使用者需要、安全、材料、维修条件、成本和时间。真实约束会迫使设计者面对取舍，并可能激发更适用的方案。约束也应接受检验：要区分不可改变的条件与未经质疑的假设。

articles.title: The Wall Where Everyone Shouted
articles.summary: To avoid offending any guild, a painter makes every part of a mural equally prominent and leaves the story without a beginning.
articles.summaryZh: 为了不得罪任何行会，画师让壁画里的每件事同样醒目，也让故事失去了开头。
storyParagraphs: The city council commissioned Baichuan to paint the story of its founding. The smiths demanded the largest furnace, the boatbuilders wanted every vessel in bright blue, and the weavers insisted that every cloth show its full pattern. Baichuan needed all the guilds to keep funding the work, so he made every figure the same height and every tool equally bright.

When the mural opened, visitors stood before it without knowing where to look first. The guide tried to begin with the lighting of the harbour's first lamp, but children stared at a golden hammer in the corner. When she reached the first ship, their eyes jumped to a row of red cloth. Every guild was visible, yet the founding story could not move forward.

After closing time, Baichuan placed small lamps in front of the wall. When the central harbour lamp was brightest, his eye landed there first, then followed the sails toward the docks and workshops. He removed no guild. Instead, he quietened distant colours, reduced repeated patterns, and turned several painted arms toward the first lamp.

The next morning, the head smith complained that his hammer had become smaller. Baichuan asked him to stand by the entrance. The first children looked at the harbour light, then the person lighting it, and finally followed the glow to the forge.
The smith said nothing more. He moved the label that had been fixed beside the golden hammer to the final section of the story.
storyParagraphsZh: 城议会请画师白川绘制建城壁画。铁匠要求自己的炉火最大，船工要每条船都用亮蓝色，织工坚持每匹布都描出花纹。白川需要各行会继续出钱，只好让每个人物一样高、每件工具一样亮。
壁画完成后，参观者站在墙前很久，却不知道先看哪里。讲解员想从点燃港口第一盏灯说起，孩子们却盯着角落里的金锤；讲到第一艘船，目光又被十几匹红布拉走。每个行会都被看见，建城故事却说不下去。
白川等到闭馆，在墙前摆了几盏小灯。他发现，只要中央的港灯更亮，人的视线便会先落在那里，再沿着船帆走向码头和工坊。他没有删掉任何行会，只把远处人物的颜色压低，减少重复花纹，并让几条手臂都朝向第一盏灯。
第二天，铁匠抱怨自己的锤子变小。白川请他站到门口。第一批孩子进来时，先看见港灯，再看到点灯的人，最后才沿着火光找到铁匠铺里的炉子。
铁匠没有再说话。他走近壁画，把原本贴在金锤上的说明牌移到了故事最后一段。
explanationParagraphs: Visual hierarchy organises the order in which elements attract attention and are understood. Scale, contrast, colour, position, spacing, direction, and detail work together to guide viewing. Hierarchy is not a ranking of moral worth, and social equality does not require identical visual emphasis. Without hierarchy, a complex composition may become unreadable.
explanationParagraphsZh: 视觉层级组织元素吸引注意和被理解的先后。尺度、对比、颜色、位置、间距、方向与细节共同引导观看。层级不等于价值排名；社会意义上的平等也不要求所有元素具有相同视觉强度。没有层级，复杂画面可能无法被清楚阅读。

articles.title: Between Two Hands
articles.summary: A painter fills a farewell scene until rain washes away one small area between its two central figures.
articles.summaryZh: 一名画家把告别画得满满当当，直到雨水洗掉了两个人之间的一小块。
storyParagraphs: Painter Shen Yao was commissioned to make a harbour farewell. She added luggage, ropes, onlookers, and warehouses in the distance, then rendered every fold in the two central figures' clothes. Each time the client visited, she said the scene did not feel like a farewell. Shen Yao responded by filling another empty place.

She extended the figures' hands toward each other and surrounded their fingertips with tickets, knots, and a travelling case. The picture became livelier, but the two people now seemed to be standing in an ordinary market. With the deadline near, Shen Yao worked through the night.

Rain entered through the roof before dawn. A drop landed between the painted hands. By the time Shen Yao woke, the tickets, rope, and background figures there had blurred away. Two hands remained, separated by a small piece of untouched wall.

She raised her brush to restore the missing details, but the client stopped in the doorway. After a long look, she said that on the day of departure, their hands had indeed failed to meet. Shen Yao erased several nearby lines and left the distance intact.
When she delivered the painting, she added only a thin wash near the wall. Between the two hands, she made no further mark.
storyParagraphsZh: 画家沈遥受托画一幅码头送别。她画上行李、缆绳、围观的人和远处的仓房，又把两位主角的衣纹描得极细。委托人看了几次，总说不像告别，沈遥便继续往空处添东西。
她让两个人伸手相握，在指尖周围又画上飘动的票据和一只提箱。画面越来越热闹，两个人却像只是站在集市里。交画期限临近，沈遥整夜没有离开画室。
凌晨漏了一场雨。水从屋顶滴下，正落在两只手之间。沈遥醒来时，那里的票据、绳结和背景人影已经晕开，只剩两只手隔着一小段没有碰到的墙面。
她举起画笔想补回去，委托人却在门口停住了。那人看了很久，说离船那天，他们最后确实没有握到手。沈遥擦掉周围多余的线，让那段距离完整留下。
交画时，她只在墙边补了一层薄色。两只手之间，没有再落下一笔。
explanationParagraphs: Negative space is the area around, between, and within depicted forms. It has shape, proportion, rhythm, and visual weight, and it changes figure-ground relationships, balance, emphasis, and meaning. It is not simply blankness or minimalism; its effect comes from its specific relationship with forms and the whole composition.
explanationParagraphsZh: 负空间是形体周围、之间与内部的区域，也具有形状、比例、节奏和视觉重量。它会改变图底关系、平衡、重点与意义。负空间不只是空白或极简风格；它的作用来自与具体形体和整体构图之间的关系。

articles.title: The Rain That Would Not Become Stone
articles.summary: A painter asks a mason to copy every transparent layer of a watercolour until real rain falls on the wall.
articles.summaryZh: 一名画家要求石匠复制水彩里的每层雨色，直到真正的雨落上石墙。
storyParagraphs: The city chose one of Shen Lan's rainy watercolours for the wall outside the station. Protective of the original, she asked the mason to reproduce it exactly: the grey roofs in the distance must remain translucent, the blue puddles must show the colour beneath, and the curtain of rain must preserve the white of the paper.

The mason tried staining the stone. Grey became muddy, blue became heavy, and transparency looked like an unfinished patch. Shen Lan repeatedly asked for thinner colour, but each wash faded in the wind. They remade the same section three times.

Rain fell before their fourth attempt. Water ran through shallow test grooves, shadows gathered in deeper cuts, rough stone held a wet shine, and polished stone reflected the sky. The mason said nothing. He placed a dry block and a wet one side by side in front of Shen Lan.

She put away her palette. Different depths of carving established distance, the stone eaves channelled real rain into the image, and polished hollows became puddles. In dry weather, the wall remained grey. When rain arrived, water lines, shadow, and reflection completed the scene.
The unveiling day was clear. Shen Lan left the original painting indoors, carried a bucket to the wall, and slowly poured water from the carved eaves.
storyParagraphsZh: 城里要把沈岚的雨景水彩刻在车站外墙上。她珍惜原画，要求石匠照样复制：远处屋顶的灰要半透明，水洼里的蓝要盖着底色，雨幕还要留出纸张透出的白。
石匠试着给石头染色。灰色浑浊，蓝色沉重，所谓透明只像没有涂完。沈岚不断要求再薄一点，颜料却一场风便褪。两个人为同一面墙返工了三次。
第四次开工前下了雨。水顺着试刻的浅沟流下来，深凿处积出暗影，粗糙表面留住水光，磨平的石面则把天空映了回去。石匠没有说话，只把一块干石和一块湿石并排放在沈岚面前。
沈岚收起调色盘。她用深浅刻痕安排远近，让屋檐把真雨导进画面，又把水洼位置磨亮。墙面干燥时只是灰石；雨一来，水线、暗影和反光才把景物补全。
揭幕那天恰好放晴。沈岚把原画留在室内，走到墙边，用一桶清水从刻出的屋檐慢慢浇下。
explanationParagraphs: Medium specificity refers to the distinctive possibilities and limits produced by a medium's material, process, conventions, and mode of viewing. Moving a work into another medium is not a matter of copying every prior effect; it requires asking how the new medium can carry, resist, or transform it. The idea need not reject mixed media, but it does require attention to material difference.
explanationParagraphsZh: 媒介特性指一种媒介的材料、过程、惯例与观看方式所提供的独特可能和限制。把作品转入另一媒介，不是逐项复制原有效果，而是判断新媒介能怎样承载、抵抗或改变它。这个概念并不排斥混合媒介，而要求创作者认真对待材料差异。
